chunks.text: Data Center segment revenue was $18.4 billion for fiscal 2025, an increase of 61% compared with $11.4 billion for fiscal 2024. Data Center revenue represented 68% of total revenue of $27.1 billion in fiscal 2025.

The increase in Data Center revenue was primarily driven by demand for our accelerated computing platforms used to train and deploy artificial intelligence models, from cloud service providers, consumer internet companies and enterprises.
Gaming segment revenue was $5.1 billion for fiscal 2025, a decrease of 4% compared with fiscal 2024, reflecting lower channel inventory levels.

Gross margin for fiscal 2025 was 71.2%, compared with 64.0% for fiscal 2024, driven by a higher mix of Data Center products. Inventory increased to $4.2 billion at fiscal year-end from $2.9 billion a year earlier.

Sales to our two largest customers, both cloud service providers, accounted for 23% and 14% of total revenue for fiscal 2025, respectively. The loss of, or a significant reduction in purchases by, either customer could materially affect our results.

Our competitors in data center accelerators include Rival Micro Devices, which began volume shipments of its RM-9 accelerator in the third quarter of fiscal 2025, as well as several of our cloud service provider customers that design accelerators for their own use.

We face intense competition, which could adversely impact our market share and financial results. The markets in which we compete are characterized by rapid technological change, evolving industry standards and new product introductions.
Several of our largest customers have announced or are developing their own custom AI accelerators, which may reduce their purchases of our products and adversely affect our Data Center revenue.
Data Center revenue for the first quarter of fiscal 2026 was $5.6 billion, up 44% from a year ago and up 3% sequentially.

CFO: We expect Data Center revenue growth to moderate in the second half of the year as several large customers digest the capacity they installed over the past year. Longer term, we continue to see strong demand for AI infrastructure.

On March 3, 2026, the Company was informed that sales of its X200 accelerator to certain regions will require an export license. Sales of affected products to those regions were approximately 9% of Data Center revenue in fiscal 2025.

Jordan Lee (Analyst): With data center revenue growing more than 80% a year, how are you thinking about supply for next year? Maria Chen (CFO): We have secured additional supply capacity for fiscal 2027 and do not expect supply to constrain us.

Rival Micro Devices began volume shipments of our RM-9 data center accelerator in fiscal 2025, and RM-9 revenue exceeded $2.0 billion in the year. We believe RM-9 offers the best performance per dollar in the industry.
